## Highlights

**A Claude Code redact install now masks MCP tools and resources by default.** In 0.14.0 `redact-claude` could mask any tool, but the installer still wrote `^(Bash|Read|Grep)$`, so MCP results reached the model unless you edited the matcher yourself. `install agent-hook claude --mode redact` and `install all --mode redact` now write `^(Bash|Read|Grep|LSP|ReadMcpResourceTool|mcp__.*)$`. `--no-mcp` keeps the hook on the built-in tools.

## Upgrade notes

Existing installs with the old matcher are reported by `doctor` as outdated: `^(Bash|Read|Grep)$` is the pre-0.14.1 default that masks only `Bash`, `Read` and `Grep`. Re-run `sekretbarilo install agent-hook claude` (with `--global` or `--settings` as before) to move the handler to the new default group, or add `--no-mcp` to keep only the built-in tools. Other handlers in the old group stay where they are.

A matcher you edited yourself is kept, as before, while it covers `Bash`, `Read` and `Grep`. Each selected call starts the sekretbarilo process: about 38 ms for a call whose response is scanned and about 3.5 ms for one that passes through, measured on one development machine.

Homebrew installs only the binary; the formula now says so after `brew install` and names the command that sets up the hooks.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`, then `sekretbarilo doctor`.

## Changes

### Claude Code hook

- The default redact matcher selects:
  - `Bash`, `Read` and `Grep`, as before;
  - `LSP`, whose `result` holds code text such as hover output or definitions;
  - `ReadMcpResourceTool`, whose `contents[].text` is MCP resource content but whose name has no `mcp__` prefix;
  - every MCP tool (`mcp__.*`), plugin-bundled MCP servers included.
- `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` are left out on purpose: external pages are full of example keys, so masking them would mostly produce false positives. `Agent`, `Write`, `Edit` and `Glob` return objects that carry no new tool output, and the hook passes them through.
- A matcher of `*`, empty or omitted is accepted and kept, but today it adds only the process cost on every other tool call.
- `redact-claude` knows the `LSP` and `ReadMcpResourceTool` shapes. It masks the string `result` of `LSP`, and the string `text` of each `contents` entry of `ReadMcpResourceTool`, and keeps `operation`, `filePath`, `uri`, `mimeType`, `blob` entries and the entry order. A response without the expected field stops the turn with the known text fields erased, as for `Bash`, `Read` and `Grep`.
- New flag `--no-mcp` for `install agent-hook claude` and `install all` writes `Bash|Read|Grep|LSP`, so MCP tools and resources are not masked. A later install without the flag keeps that matcher; an explicit `--no-mcp` narrows `*`, the default or any custom matcher. It applies to redact mode only: with `--mode block`, or when the omitted mode resolves to `block` (a block hook is installed, or nothing is), the command fails and writes nothing, and `install all` fails before its pre-commit step. Codex is unaffected. Elsewhere `--no-mcp` is a usage error.
- After a redact install the installer prints the scope, and `doctor` adds it to the line of a current redact hook: `all tools`, `Bash, Read, Grep, LSP and MCP tools and resources`, `Bash, Read, Grep, LSP only (--no-mcp)`, or `custom matcher <m>`.

### Homebrew

- The formula gains caveats: no hooks are installed by `brew`; `sekretbarilo install all --global --mode redact` is the recommended setup, masking Bash, Read, Grep, LSP and MCP tool output, with `--no-mcp` to keep only the built-in tools; `sekretbarilo doctor` checks the result.

### Known limits

- Tools a plugin registers without an MCP server still fire no `PostToolUse` hook in Claude Code, so no matcher reaches them.
- The `blob` of an MCP resource and non-text content blocks are not scanned.
